setup_summary.text: Salesforce reports fiscal Q3 FY27 (quarter ended Oct 31) on Dec 1 after the close. Consensus is $11.57B revenue (+12.8% y/y) and $3.47 EPS. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±6.8%. No options-implied move or whisper number exists yet, and the beat/miss record could not be retrieved.

Q2 FY27 revenue was $11.345B (+10.8% y/y). Operating income was flat at $2.33B, so GAAP operating margin fell to 20.5% from 22.8%. Gross margin slipped to about 76.7% from 78.1%. Amortization of acquired intangibles rose to $522M from $380M, and restructuring to $94M from $4M. Together those two items explain about 2 of the 2.3 points of margin decline, by my arithmetic.

Headline growth is flattered by Informatica, which added about $456M in Q2 (about 4.5 points). Excluding it, Q2 growth was about +6.4%. It was acquired in Nov 2025 and is absent from the Q3 FY26 base of $10.26B. If it contributes about 4.5 points again, the consensus of $11.57B (+12.8%) needs about 8.3 points from everything else (organic, Qualified, Fin, Contentful), versus about 6.4 in Q2. This split is my arithmetic, not a company figure.

The 20% growth in 'Data 360, Headless Platform and Other' ($3,618M vs $3,008M) is mostly Informatica, which the 10-Q groups in that line. Removing its roughly $456M of revenue leaves about +5%. Agentforce Apps grew about 8% ($7,193M vs $6,682M). The AI-led reacceleration story is therefore not yet visible in reported segment growth.

Current RPO was $33.5B, up 14% y/y. Total RPO was $66.3B, up 11% y/y and down from $72.4B at Jan 31 (seasonal, because Q4 carries the heaviest renewals). Q2 billings and other were $9,769M versus $8,992M a year earlier, about +8.6%, which is slower than revenue growth of 10.8%.

The balance sheet changed sharply. Debt principal was $39.5B versus $14.5B at Jan 31, against cash and securities of $11.4B. A $25B ASR was funded with March 2026 notes. Interest expense was $473M in Q2 versus $67M, and diluted shares were 821M versus 962M. Operating cash flow was $1.27B in Q2 and free cash flow about $1.1B.

Q2 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.29 included a $2.613B pre-tax gain on strategic investments, of which $2.7B was unrealized Anthropic gains. Anthropic is about $5.1B, or 45%, of the $11.3B portfolio. At the 10-Q's 23.5% rate, the gain is about $2.43 per share, so ex-gain GAAP EPS was about $1.86. This is my calculation from the filing.

Deals: Fin (Intercom, about $3.6B) closed Sept 10, and Contentful (about $1.5B, net of shares already owned) has been reported as completed. The 10-Q expected both to close in Q3. Braze (about $5.66B EV, $47.50 cash per share) was announced Oct 20 and is expected to close in FY28.

last_reported.text: Q2 FY27 revenue was $11.345B (+10.8% y/y), of which Informatica was about $456M.

view.text: The guide of $11.42–11.50B (+11.3% to +12.1%) comes from August press summaries, not a primary release. Consensus sits about $70M (0.6%) above its top. Q2 revenue beat consensus by only about 0.25%, so $11.57B needs a larger-than-usual beat or a bigger Fin/Contentful contribution than the roughly 0.5 point I assume. I model $11.50–11.58B. Revenue is a low-odds beat versus consensus and a likely beat versus the guide.

last_reported.text: At Q2, cRPO was $33.5B (+14% y/y), with minimal FX effect. At Jan 31 it was +16% reported, including about 3 points of FX tailwind.

consensus.text: No analyst consensus was found. A thinly traded Polymarket market (Oct 24) put roughly 42% on 16–17%, 27% on 15–16% and 10% on 14–15%, versus a guide of about 14% in constant currency. Volume per bucket was only about $0.9–2.6k.

view.text: The ~14% guide reportedly excluded Fin and Contentful before close, per Aug 31 press. Both closed in Q3, so reported cRPO should include them and could print well above 14%. Judge organic acceleration only on an organic or constant-currency figure ex-acquisitions, which management must supply. A headline 16%+ would not by itself show demand acceleration.

last_reported.text: Q2 GAAP diluted EPS was $4.29, or about $1.86 ex the investment gain. Non-GAAP EPS was $5.90, of which about $2.53 was the gain per Aug press, leaving about $3.37.

consensus.text: Consensus EPS is $3.47. The basis (GAAP or non-GAAP) is not stated, but the number only fits a non-GAAP, ex-gain basis. The fact sheet's +58.5% growth compares it with a GAAP $2.19 base, which is apples to oranges.

view.text: The guide of $3.42–3.44 (press) is $0.03–0.05 below consensus, which is $0.10 above the Q2 ex-gain run-rate of $3.37. Lower interest income on about $5B of deal cash and a full quarter of $25B note coupons offset the ASR share-count benefit. A print of $3.45–3.52 looks plausible. The risk is that consensus has drifted above guidance.

last_reported.text: The Q2 gain was $2.613B pre-tax. Q2 also had $285M of impairments. Six-month gain per share was $2.87.

view.text: Model no Anthropic mark in Q3 and treat any GAAP print as noise. The last priced round was $965B in May, and the IPO prospectus was reported Oct 26 with no shares trading, so a Q3 mark-up is unlikely. The 10-Q says private marks are booked only on observable same-issuer transactions or impairment. A 10% enterprise-value fall in the five largest holdings would cut carrying value by about $641M. As an illustration only, if a $1.5–2T IPO were an observable price, Anthropic's roughly $5.1B carrying value would imply a $2.8–5.5B pre-tax mark, on a crude linear scaling that ignores share-class rights. That would land in Q4 or later.

last_reported.text: Q2 GAAP operating margin was 20.5% (22.8% a year earlier).

view.text: Scheduled amortization is $839M for the remaining six months of FY27, about $420M a quarter versus $522M in Q2. Restructuring is not expected to recur at scale (Q2 was $94M). Together that is worth about 1.5–2 points of GAAP margin before the new Fin/Contentful amortization and opex. Expect sequential GAAP margin recovery, with dilution risk from the acquisitions.

last_reported.text: Q2 interest expense was $473M (Q1 about $317M, derived as the six-month $790M less Q2). Other income was $81M versus $135M a year earlier.

view.text: Q2 is a full-quarter run-rate for the March 2026 notes and term loan. Model about $470–480M of interest expense. Other income should fall further as about $5B of cash goes to Fin and Contentful. The company said the March notes will push interest expense above the prior year throughout FY27.

last_reported.text: Q2 diluted shares were 821M. Another 42M weighted shares of unsettled ASR forward were excluded as anti-dilutive. About 823M shares were outstanding on Aug 20.

view.text: The ASR delivered about 103M shares, roughly 80% of the total expected, so about 26M shares remain at an implied $194 average price. Final settlement is due in Q3. An October settlement and a $176 'to date' price come from Sept press and are unverified. The late-quarter delivery trims Q3 weighted shares by only about 4–6M, worth about $0.02–0.03 of EPS. The fuller benefit lands in Q4, with a base roughly 3–5% below Q2's 821M.

since_filing.text: On Oct 20 Salesforce signed a deal to buy Braze for about $5.66B EV ($47.50 cash per share). Closing is expected in FY28. The 8-K says there is no anticipated change to FY27 guidance, no FY28 guidance, and no long-term target update. The company expects to fund the deal with cash and flags near-term profitability dilution.

The market reaction to Braze was mild for Salesforce. CRM slipped roughly 1% on the day (an early indication was -2.6%) while Braze jumped more than 50%. The price is about 58% above Braze's prior close and about 7x its $738M trailing revenue. Braze has a net loss of about $131M.

Fin closed on Sept 10, and Contentful has been reported as completed. Salesforce also bought Loops on Oct 12. Both closings land in the quarter being reported, so Q3 will carry their first revenue, cash outflows, amortization and integration costs, and the print has more inorganic content than the guide's organic framing.

On Oct 29 CRM fell about 4.5% (-4.46% per TradingKey, -4.6% per Benzinga), with IGV down 3.3% and Workday down about 4%. The trigger was ServiceNow's worst day on record, on a slowdown in contracted backlog. An intraday quote of $229.92 (-5.03%) implies a prior close near $242. The sector move was about four times the Braze-day move.

ServiceNow's 10-Q shows Q3 revenue +21% y/y ($4.1B) and subscription revenue +21%, yet the stock fell sharply on backlog growth. Investors are therefore punishing forward-indicator deceleration even when reported growth is strong. That makes Salesforce's cRPO the key line on Dec 1. No Microsoft, Adobe or Workday results were retrieved.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus was reported Oct 26. The last private round was $965B in May, the IPO target is $1.5–2T, and shares were not yet trading as of Oct 26–29. No newer priced round was reported, so a Q3 mark-up is unlikely and the Anthropic mark is more of a Q4+ event.

A prediction market on Salesforce Q3 cRPO growth (constant currency, resolving Dec 2) put about 42% on 16–17%, 27% on 15–16% and 10% on 14–15%, versus the ~14% guide. The market is thin (about $0.9–2.6k per bucket), so treat it as a loose sentiment gauge, not a consensus.

key_debates.question: Is organic growth re-accelerating, or is headline growth just Informatica and M&A?

bull.text: Current RPO grew 14% y/y, higher than Q2's roughly 11% total revenue growth ex-FX effects would imply. Management reiterated second-half organic reacceleration, and the market is positioned for cRPO of 15%+.

bear.text: Ex-Informatica, Q2 growth was only about 6.4%, Data 360 ex-Informatica about 5%, and Agentforce Apps about 8%. Billings grew about 8.6%. Consensus of $11.57B needs about 8.3 points of non-Informatica growth versus about 6.4 in Q2, and it sits above the top of the guide.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Dec 1 organic or constant-currency growth figure with Fin and Contentful stripped out, the revenue bridge between acquired and organic, and cRPO ex-acquisitions versus the guided ~14%.

key_debates.question: How much of the reported cRPO trend is demand versus FX and acquisitions?

bull.text: At Jan 31, 16% reported cRPO growth included about 3 points of FX. Q2's 14% had minimal FX, so constant-currency growth rose from about 13% to 14% (my arithmetic).

bear.text: On a reported basis cRPO growth slowed from 16% to 14%. Fin and Contentful closed in Q3 and were excluded from the ~14% guide, so a higher reported number may be purchased growth. Total RPO fell to $66.3B from $72.4B.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Reported versus constant-currency versus organic cRPO growth disclosed side by side on Dec 1.

key_debates.question: How should investors treat GAAP EPS quality and the Anthropic stake?

bull.text: The Anthropic stake is about $5.1B (45% of the portfolio). If it is marked toward an IPO target of $1.5–2T, the value could rise materially above its carrying amount, supporting buybacks or debt paydown.

bear.text: Q2 GAAP EPS of $4.29 included a $2.6B pre-tax gain on strategic investments, and the company says strategic investment gains lifted six-month diluted EPS by $2.87. The portfolio is concentrated, the five largest holdings carry about $641M of sensitivity per 10% enterprise-value move, and Q2 also had $285M of impairments.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gains/losses line (expected near zero for Anthropic), the Anthropic IPO pricing date, and whether management guides on an ex-gain basis.

key_debates.question: Does serial M&A and a debt-funded buyback create value or dilute margins?

bull.text: Management says deals meet its M&A framework, expects to fund Braze with cash (a non-dilutive form of consideration), and cites growth accretion balanced by near-term profitability dilution. The ASR cut diluted shares from 962M to 821M year on year, and six-month operating cash flow grew 10.4%.

bear.text: Debt principal is $39.5B versus $14.5B in January, interest expense is $473M a quarter, and about $10.8B of Contentful, Fin and Braze cash is roughly equal to the entire $11.4B of cash. The company flags near-term profitability dilution, and Q2 operating income was flat on 10.8% revenue growth.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 and FY28 margin commentary, net debt after Q3 acquisitions, and any leverage or credit-rating statement (none found).

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Revenue of $11.58B or more (at or above consensus), cRPO growth of 15–16%+ with a credible organic figure of 14%+ ex-acquisitions, non-GAAP EPS of $3.50+, and a raised FY27 guide with a margin-neutral deal bridge. After the Oct 29 de-rating, the average closing move of ±6.8% skews upward.

triggers: Reported and organic cRPO growth above the ~14% guide
Revenue above $11.57B with disclosed Fin/Contentful contribution of $60M or less
FY27 raise beyond the deal contribution
Confirmation of FY30 framework and positive FY28 colour

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue of $11.50–11.57B, near the top of the guide but below consensus. Reported cRPO is 14–16% (lifted by Fin and Contentful) with organic about 14%, non-GAAP EPS of $3.44–3.50, and FY27 guidance held or nudged for deal contributions. GAAP EPS comes out near $1.8–1.9 with no meaningful investment gains. The stock trades on the Q4/FY28 outlook.

triggers: ASR final settlement disclosed with the remaining shares delivered

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue near or below the top of the guide ($11.50B or less) with organic growth around 6%, cRPO at or below 14% once acquisitions are stripped out, billings lagging revenue again, and cautious Q4 guidance reflecting Braze/Fin dilution. After ServiceNow's backlog-driven plunge, a soft cRPO could trigger a double-digit move.

triggers: Margin guide lowered for acquisition costs

claim.text: AI disruption of seat-based software. The 10-Q lists AI-native competitors that may bypass traditional workflows. The Oct 29 sector selloff (CRM -4.5%, IGV -3.3%) shows how fast sentiment turns on any forward-indicator deceleration.

Leverage and acquisition integration. Debt principal is $39.5B, and Contentful, Fin and Braze add about $10.8B of cash needs against $11.4B of cash. The acquisition risk factor cites the Informatica financing, and management flags near-term profitability dilution on Braze.

Strategic-investment concentration and volatility. Anthropic is about 45% of the $11.3B portfolio (22% at Jan 31, and two holdings were 35% in the 10-K). The 10-Q warns that gains and losses could be material and that private marks depend on observable transactions or impairment.

ASR settlement uncertainty. The 10-Q now says stock-price volatility may obligate Salesforce to deliver shares or make a cash payment on final settlement. That language is not in the 10-K. The remaining share delivery and any cash true-up depend on the final average price.

Dependence on third-party frontier AI models and AI-enabled security threats. The 10-Q adds that access to frontier models may be suspended or restricted by providers or governments, and that frontier AI may help attackers find zero-day flaws faster. Neither is in the 10-K.

Backpage litigation keeps growing, with new plaintiff groups added since the 10-K (for example E.Y.W. and F.P., plus many N.D. Cal. cases). Most actions are stayed pending criminal proceedings. The company cannot estimate a loss range. The 10-K's expected Fall 2026 trial date in G.G. does not appear in the 10-Q.

Mix and demand weakness in professional services and license-type revenue. Professional services fell 4% on lower demand for larger multi-year transformation engagements, which 'may continue'. Term licenses were about 4% of subscription revenue versus 6% a year ago.

questions_for_management.question: What is the organic, constant-currency cRPO growth in Q3 excluding Fin and Contentful, and how much of reported cRPO growth comes from the two deals?

why.text: The ~14% guide reportedly excluded both deals, which closed in Q3, and the prediction market is positioned for 15–17%. Without an organic split, a high headline would be uninterpretable.

questions_for_management.question: What did Fin and Contentful contribute to Q3 revenue, and what is their expected FY27 contribution inside the $46.1–46.4B guide?

why.text: The FY27 raise reportedly includes $200M from the two deals, but consensus ($11.57B) sits above the guided Q3 range and the revenue bridge is unclear.

questions_for_management.question: When did the ASR settle, how many shares were delivered, at what final average price, and was there any cash or share true-up?

why.text: About 103M shares (about 80%) were delivered up front. The remainder, roughly 26M at an implied $194 average, drives Q4 share count, and the 10-Q says price volatility may require shares or cash.

questions_for_management.question: How will Braze be funded, what happens to net debt and leverage after about $10.8B of deal cash, and have rating agencies commented?

why.text: Cash is $11.4B against $39.5B of debt. The release says Braze will be cash-funded, and the 10-Q lists credit-rating downgrades as a risk. No agency commentary was found.

questions_for_management.question: What is the expected margin path including Braze, Fin and Contentful, and does the FY30 framework still hold once these deals are included?

why.text: Operating margin fell to 20.5% from 22.8%, the Braze release flags 'near term profitability dilution', and the FY30 framework is unchanged only 'at this time'.

questions_for_management.question: Does management plan to monetize or hold the Anthropic stake, and how will an IPO be marked in the accounts and in non-GAAP guidance?

why.text: Anthropic is about $5.1B (45%) of the portfolio. Strategic investment gains lifted six-month GAAP EPS by $2.87, and an IPO at $1.5–2T could drive a large mark.

data_gaps: Primary text of the Aug 26 earnings release and call (Q3 guide, GAAP Q3 EPS guide, FY27 EPS wording, acquisition treatment) could not be opened. All Q3 and FY27 guidance numbers rest on August press summaries, which are older than 14 days.
The basis of the $3.47 consensus (GAAP vs non-GAAP) is not stated, and the fact sheet's +58.5% EPS growth compares it with a GAAP $2.19 base. The Q3 FY26 non-GAAP EPS base was not in the sources.
The August consensus ($11.42B / $3.39) could not be confirmed, so it is unclear whether consensus has risen above guidance since August or when.
Q1 FY27 cRPO growth (reported and constant currency) is missing, so the 16% to Q1 to 14% path is incomplete. Informatica's contribution to y/y cRPO growth is not disclosed.
Fin and Contentful revenue, cRPO and close-date details (Contentful's exact date) are not available, so the inorganic share of Q3 is my estimate.

ASR final settlement date, final average price and any cash true-up are unknown. The $176 average price and 'at least 14%' language come from Sept press (24/7 Wall St.) citing the Aug 26 release, which was not retrieved.

No analyst rating or price-target changes dated Oct 20–31 were found for CRM (only September target raises). Microsoft, Adobe and Workday quarterly results were not retrieved. No rating-agency actions were found.

Agentforce ARR (above $1.5B) and AI-and-data ARR (about $3.9B) are from secondary August coverage and were not verified against primary text. No verified Dreamforce or Investor Day update on FY30 targets was found.
No options-implied move, whisper EPS, or historical beat/miss record is available. The CRM closing prices for Oct 29–31 are not established.
